title: Listing publication governance playbook
content:
Purpose:
This lightweight playbook defines the cross-functional gates, required assets, and copy guidance for publishing Redwood Inference listings across cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP). It is intended to be a practical preflight checklist for Partner Managers, Product Marketers, and Engineering Owners during publisher onboarding and listing publication.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to commercial marketplace listings where Redwood is the publisher or co-publisher of the product offering.
- Excludes internal partner portal drafts and third-party reseller listings (those have separate ops flows).
- Assumes partner has completed legal DPAs and has an approved reseller agreement (if required).

Quick summary of acceptance gates (must be green to publish):
1) Content & Messaging: approved tile, 1-liner, 150-word summary, full feature bullets, and 3 vendor-approved screenshots.
2) Technical Integration: connector validated end-to-end (deploy/test/acceptance), telemetry and usage reporting hooks present.
3) Pricing & Entitlements: SKU mapping complete, trial/credit logic verified, billing SKU tested in sandbox.
4) Security & Compliance: SOC2 status and data residency notes present; any customer-managed-key (CMK) flows documented.
5) Legal & Marketplace Policy: terms-of-service alignment, export control check, acceptable use language in copy.
6) Observability & Support: support contact, SLA tier mapping, and on-call rotation for first 30 days.

Detailed preflight checklist (copy + assets) — owner: Product Marketing
- Short title (<= 55 chars) — SKU-safe, avoid trademark overflow.
- One-line subtitle / elevator pitch (<= 120 chars) — benefit first, avoid technical jargon.
- 150-word summary (marketing friendly) + 300–600 word long-form description for docs page.
- 5–6 feature bullet points (30–60 chars each) focusing on operational benefits: latency, cost controls, private deployments, SLA, observability.
- Three screenshots: console dashboard (token-cost view), model selection UI, rollout policy config. Add captions.
- 2 short customer benefit quotes (if available) or placeholder B2B value props.
- CTA variants: Get started (free credits), Request demo (enterprise), Contact sales (custom contracts).
- Accessibility check: alt text for images, color contrast for screenshots.

Technical acceptance checklist — owner: Engineering (solutions/ops)
- Connector verification in marketplace sandbox: provisioning flow completes + logs captured.
- API keys / auth flows exercised: token exchange, scoped tokens for marketplace-managed accounts.
- Entitlement mapping: SKU -> Redwood product id mapping documented and tested in billing simulator.
- Usage/telemetry hooks: metering events emitted, ingestion to billing pipeline validated (sample events captured for 3 distinct flows).
- E2E upgrade & rollback test: can push listing changes without impacting live customers in dedicated capacity.
- Sample test cases: create instance, route requests to hosted API, verify model variant fallback.

Security & compliance — owner: Security/Legal
- Confirm applicable compliance badges (SOC2, ISO27001) and their visibility in listing.
- Data residency note: must include region notes for Private deployments.
- KMS/HSM integration: document CMK availability and constraints.
- Privacy blurb: telemetry and metrics collection + opt-out/pseudonymization text.
- Export control / restricted countries check (list any exclusions).

Pricing, SKUs, and entitlements — owner: Finance/Product
- SKU naming convention: product.env.capacity (e.g., inference.hosted.small).
- Pricing variants documented: pay-as-you-go (per-token), committed (monthly reserved throughput), enterprise list (annual).
- Trial & credits: free credits redemption flow documented and verified with marketplace sandbox.
- Quantity vs unit definition: token vs embed-unit; ensure mapping to marketplace metering unit.
- Billing test: simulate invoice generation and verify line items match SKU naming.

Observability & support — owner: Customer Success / SRE
- Support contact and escalation path included in listing metadata.
- On-call schedule for first 30 days after publish: rostering + contact card.
- Instrumentation check: error rates, latency percentiles surfaced in console tile.
- Post-publish health check cadence: daily for first week, weekly for month 1, then standard.

Marketplace copy guidance (examples and do-not-say) — owner: PMM
- DO: "Predictable latency and cost controls for LLM inference"; focus on outcomes.
- DO: Short example: "Ship LLM features with 99% P99 latency under 200ms (typical)." (only if validated).
- DO NOT: use absolute capability claims that are unverified (e.g., "fastest in market"), or compare directly to named competitors in copy.

Suggested copy snippets (short/long):
- 1-line: "Redwood Inference — predictable, production-ready LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- 150-word summary: "Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime for serving large language models at production scale. Ship features faster with predictable latency, transparent cost controls, and enterprise-grade tooling for rollouts and observability. Choose hosted API for rapid prototyping, Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, or Private deployments for data sovereignty. Supported features include streaming responses, function/tool calling, and model variant rollouts with automatic fallbacks. Get started with free credits and built-in monitoring to validate performance against your SLA."

Rollout & publishing plan (timeline, owner responsibilities):
- T-21 days: finalize copy and screenshots, legal sign-off on terms (Owner: PMM, Legal).
- T-14 days: engineering completes marketplace connector verification + billing tests (Owner: Solutions Eng).
- T-7 days: field trial with 2 pilot customers (Owner: CS + Sales).
- T-3 days: SRE readiness check, on-call posted, observability dashboards published.
- Go-live day: confirm sync of SKUs, enable listing in marketplace (Owner: GTM operations).
- Post-launch week 1: daily health check & first-week incident response window (Owner: SRE / CS).

Risk register (top items to monitor):
- Billing misalignment (SKU naming mismatch -> failed invoices). Mitigation: preflight billing test and invoice sample.
- Overpromised latency guarantees. Mitigation: include conservative ranges and monitor P95/P99 by token type.
- Marketplace policy rejection due to phrasing. Mitigation: involve marketplace policy manager early and keep competitor-free language.

Open questions: (who owns answers; resolve before T-14)
- Should trial redemption be automatic or require sales acceptance for enterprise SKUs? (Owner: Finance + Sales)
- How to surface private-deployment pricing differences in the single listing (single SKU vs separate listings)? (Owner: Product + Finance)
- Are there legal constraints on including customer logos in listing pages? (Owner: Legal)

Next steps & owner map:
- PMM: finalize copy + alt text + captions (Aisha) — due: 2025-11-10 (done in draft).
- Engineering: connector acceptance + telemetry spec (Ravi) — due: 2025-11-18.
- Finance: SKU mapping doc and billing simulator run (Claire) — due: 2025-11-20.
- Legal: marketplace terms sign-off + export control check (Jordan) — due: 2025-11-14.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a condensed playbook meant to be executable; if you need a full runbook for each marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP) I will expand into vendor-specific checklists that cover UI field mappings and screenshots required by each portal.
- If you see a missing cross-functional owner, flag inline and I'll add to owner map.

Keywords for searching: publisher onboarding, marketplace preflight, SKU mapping, partner listing checklist.

End of doc.
